title: Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo - Skyline Search
summary: Intro + hosted embeddings and rerank demo with Skyline Search. Covered current vector store, sample latency/cost targets, security (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and a proposed pilot. Agreed next steps: security docs, pricing sheet, trial keys and a 2-week POC kickoff next Tuesday.
transcript:
00:00 Liam Carter: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we got about 40 minutes on the calendar. quick intros?
00:08 Aisha Khan: hi i'm aisha, head of search at Skyline, we own relevance for product search.
00:12 Tom Reyes: Tom, lead ML eng, mostly responsible for embeddings pipeline.
00:16 Sophie Li: Sophie, SRE, i'll be helping with infra and networking questions.
00:20 Maya Patel: Maya from Redwood, i'll do the demo and dig into perf details.
00:24 Liam Carter: great, want to start with a quick runbook: current stack, main pain, and success metrics please.
00:33 Aisha Khan: sure, so right now we're on Elastic/OpenSearch for indexing, using an in-house embedding pipeline with a small transformer from huggingface, and a Pinecone demo for vectors. our main issue is re-ranking quality at scale and the cost is spiking when we do more recall. latency SLOs are 200ms P50, 400ms P95 for the rerank step.
00:55 Tom Reyes: also throughput, we're seeing spikes during campaigns, tens of qps to a few hundred qps. we don't want to manage GPUs ourselves if avoidable.
01:05 Liam Carter: ok makes sense. question on current vector store: is Pinecone the canonical store or you have an internal Redis/FAISS?
01:12 Tom Reyes: we keep faiss for batch offline and pinecone for online; but data residency is a concern for some EU markets.
01:20 Maya Patel: thanks — we'll touch on hosted vs dedicated and VPC options. quick callout: hosted API supports embeddings + a rerank endpoint that does a two-stage search: initial candidate retrieval (your ES/OpenSearch) then embeddings-based rerank using our hosted model.
01:40 Maya Patel: demo plan: show embeddings API, the rerank endpoint, console for scoring distributions, and our Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization) for cost.
01:49 Liam Carter: cool, go ahead.
01:55 Maya Patel: (screen share) okay first, here's the simple embeddings call... sample payload, response vector, note we surface model id, vector dim and quality profile.
02:10 Maya Patel: (slight pause) there may be some mis-transcripts in the auto notes — ignore 'KV cash' in the slide, it's 'KV cache'.
02:20 Tom Reyes: what models do you host? are they open like Mistral/Meta or custom redwood models?
02:27 Maya Patel: we host a catalog of curated open models, and we publish performance profiles. for embeddings we recommend rwd-embed-qa-v1 for semantic search work, but you can switch to other dims.
02:36 Aisha Khan: what's the token cost for rerank vs plain retrieval?
02:40 Liam Carter: (answers) rerank cost depends on model size and number of candidates. our Optimize product will recommend batching and cache TTLs to reduce unit cost, plus you can use lightweight embed models for candidate filtering.
02:52 Maya Patel: demo: now hitting the rerank endpoint — you POST query + candidate ids + candidate embeddings optional, and we return re-ordered results with per-document scores and explainability snippet.
03:10 Sophie Li: do you stream the rerank response?
03:13 Maya Patel: currently rerank returns final ranking JSON, not streaming; generation APIs stream. rerank is low-latency synchronous.
03:20 Tom Reyes: latency numbers? with 50 candidates?
03:24 Maya Patel: in our hosted benchmarks on g4-equivalent runtime, 50-candidate rerank with rwd-embed-qa-v1 average ~85ms P50, ~210ms P95; your mileage varies with doc length and candidate embedding retrieval time.
03:42 Tom Reyes: that P95 is decent. how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? our current pipeline has repeated queries for similar sessions.
03:50 Maya Patel: we support prefix/KV cache for generation workloads; for rerank specifically, Optimize suggests caching embeddings for frequently updated docs and using request-level cache for identical queries.
04:04 Aisha Khan: can we host this in our VPC? we have strict data controls for EU.
04:09 Liam Carter: yes, we offer Redwood Private — VPC and on-prem options — with customer-managed networking and KMS integration. for many teams they start hosted and then move to dedicated or private for data residency.
04:22 Sophie Li: for VPC, is SAML SSO and IAM supported?
04:25 Maya Patel: yes SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. we also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and have SOC2 Type II.
04:34 Tom Reyes: curious about logs — do you retain raw request text in hosted? we need to ensure PII is not stored.
04:38 Liam Carter: by default hosted stores request logs for troubleshooting, but you can opt-out or configure redaction and retention. we can provide contracts and a data processing addendum for EU specifics.
04:51 Aisha Khan: good. can you show the console view for token-level cost and rollouts?
04:56 Maya Patel: yes — (switch) here's the Console Cost tab, per-route breakdown, embed usage over time, and a rollout we did for canary model switching with automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes.
05:15 Tom Reyes: interesting. for the rerank step, do you support hybrid scoring (BM25 + embed score fusion)?
05:22 Maya Patel: absolutely, rerank accepts multiple score inputs and does configurable fusion weights. you can pass BM25 scores from your ES and we combine them with semantic scores.
05:32 Aisha Khan: that could help our edge cases. on infra cost, what's the expected monthly for a 100k queries/month consumer with 5-doc rerank per query?
05:42 Liam Carter: pricing varies, but we have a baseline hosted plan; we'll follow up with a pricing sheet. Optimize will also give recommendations like using 128-d embeddings for filtering and a heavier model only for final rerank to reduce cost.
05:58 Tom Reyes: about throughput spikes — do you do autoscaling and burst capacity?
06:02 Maya Patel: yes hosted supports autoscaling; Dedicated reserves GPU pools with predictable throughput and burst. Smart routing can also move traffic to cheaper regions/models if needed.
06:16 Sophie Li: network egress concerns — any guidance for minimizing?
06:19 Liam Carter: colocating rerank in same region as your candidate store helps; we can set up private peering for dedicated and private deployments to reduce egress.
06:29 Aisha Khan: can we run a quick bench? say we hand you a sample 10k queries and candidate set, can Redwood run a benchmark?
06:35 Maya Patel: yes we can run a sandbox benchmark; typical next step is provide sample data, we'll run hosted benchmarks and share performance/cost spreadsheet.
06:45 Tom Reyes: for the POC, our main success metrics: improve MRR (mean reciprocal rank) by 10% on product search, P95 latency <= 400ms, and cost under $X per thousand reranks — we need rough numbers in the pricing.
06:58 Liam Carter: noted. i'll capture those as POC success criteria.
07:04 Maya Patel: demo continued: Optimize tab — we show recommendations: batching tokens per request, using per-route cache TTL, suggested quantization for on-prem. note: quantization recommendations are model-specific.
07:20 Aisha Khan: you mentioned model variants and fallback — how seamless is fallback when capacity's constrained?
07:25 Maya Patel: seamless — Smart routing will route to a compatible variant with similar embedding dim. if an unavailable model is requested, we can automatically fall back to the pinned variant and emit alerts.
07:38 Tom Reyes: any known issues with re-ranking very long docs? our product descriptions can be long.
07:42 Maya Patel: long docs increase tokenization cost; we typically recommend truncation schemes or chunking with BM25 pre-score then rerank on snippets.
07:50 Sophie Li: what's the typical onboarding time for a POC?
07:53 Liam Carter: for a hosted POC we can get you trial keys and a basic integration within 1 week; dedicated or private takes longer (weeks for VPC config).
08:01 Aisha Khan: ok that's realistic.
08:05 Tom Reyes: security docs?
08:07 Liam Carter: we'll share SOC2 report, encryption whitepaper, and our DPA — i'll drop links.
08:12 Maya Patel: demo wrap: here's a live request example (skipped minute details) — response shows per-doc vector similarity scores and a confidence band. note sometimes the ASR picks up 're-rank' as 'rerank' consistently spelled but examples may differ.
08:30 Aisha Khan: quick clarifying Q: can we send candidate embeddings instead of letting you fetch from a store?
08:34 Maya Patel: yes you can pass candidate embeddings; that avoids a fetch and reduces end-to-end latency. most customers do that when they already have embeddings cached in their app.
08:44 Tom Reyes: how do you handle schema for explainability snippets? we need traceability for ranking decisions.
08:49 Maya Patel: rerank returns per-doc features and a short explainability token — it's not a full model dump but enough to audit decisions. we also provide trace logs in the Console for each request id.
09:03 Sophie Li: do you expose request ids for tracing?
09:05 Maya Patel: yes, every response includes request_id and trace link if you have Console access.
09:12 Aisha Khan: ok this looks promising. can you summarize the POC scope and timeline?
09:16 Liam Carter: sure — propose: 2-week hosted trial, we'll send trial API keys, you send 10k sample queries + candidate sets, we'll run bench and return results and a cost/latency spreadsheet. goal: validate MRR uplift and P95 latency under 400ms.
09:36 Tom Reyes: fine. any blockers on our side? schema export and data redaction are questions but manageable.
09:42 Liam Carter: next steps i'll email security pack + pricing + trial keys; maya will run the sandbox bench and share spreadsheet; schedule a 30min POC kickoff next Tuesday.
09:56 Aisha Khan: sounds good.
10:00 Maya Patel: final notes: competitors often mentioned in our calls are Pinecone and Weaviate for vector DB or Elastic hybrid solutions, and folks sometimes compare to self-hosted FAISS; we can show comparative notes later.
10:18 Liam Carter: ok we'll wrap. thanks all.
10:22 (meeting ended)
